propositions.text: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the RAD decision dismissing his appeal from the RPD decision.
propositions.quote: Mr. Francisco Javier Nieves Velazquez (the “Applicant”) seeks judicial review of a decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Appeal Division (the “RAD”), dismissing his appeal from a decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Protection Division (the “RPD”).

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the RAD decision dismissing his appeal from the RPD decision, the court states.

propositions.text: The Applicant is a Mexican citizen who operated a watermelon farm with his father in Veracruz.
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Mexico. Together with his father he operated a watermelon farm in the state of Veracruz.

propositions.text: On March 10, 2021, two armed CJNG members demanded money and threatened the Applicant not to report to police.
propositions.quote: On March 10, 2021, two armed members of the Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generacion (the “CJNG”) demanded money and told him that he was expected to pay money every month. He was threatened that if he reported to the police, they would know about it.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant is a Mexican citizen who farmed in Veracruz and was threatened by CJNG members to pay money monthly, the court states.

propositions.text: In October 2021, the CJNG demanded increased payment which the Applicant could not pay.
propositions.quote: In October 21, the CJNG demanded increased payment. The Applicant did not have funds to pay the demand.

paragraphs.summary: In October 2021, the CJNG demanded increased payment which the Applicant could not pay, the court states.

propositions.text: In February 2022, the Applicant was beaten and threatened with abduction by CJNG men for not paying extortion.
propositions.quote: In February 2022, when the Applicant did not have money to pay the extortion demands, the CJNG sent two men to his house. He was beaten and threatened with abduction if he did not pay.

propositions.text: The Applicant paid extortion until December 1, 2022.
propositions.quote: The Applicant paid the extortion until December 1, 2022.

paragraphs.summary: In February 2022, the Applicant was beaten and threatened by CJNG men and paid extortion until December 1, 2022, the court states.

propositions.text: The Applicant left home on November 27, 2022, stayed with in-laws in Veracruz, and left Mexico on January 20, 2023.
propositions.quote: The Applicant left his home on November 27, 2022, and went to stay with his in-laws in another town in Veracruz. He left Mexico on January 20, 2023.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant left home on November 27, 2022, stayed with in-laws, and left Mexico on January 20, 2023, the court states.

propositions.text: After the Applicant left Mexico, CJNG left threatening envelopes at his house; his wife and children moved to her family.
propositions.quote: Following his departure from Mexico, his wife told him that the CJNG had left envelopes at his house, threatening his children. His wife and children left their house and moved to her family.

paragraphs.summary: After the Applicant left Mexico, CJNG threatened his children and his family moved to her family, the court states.

propositions.text: The RAD agreed with the RPD that the Applicant was credible, CJNG could find him nationwide, and an Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) to Meridian in Yucatan is available.
propositions.quote: The RAD agreed with the findings of the RPD: that the Applicant was credible, that the CJNG had the ability to find him throughout the country, and that he could safely relocate to Meridian in Yucatan state. This means that an Internal Flight Alternative (“IFA”) is available to him.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD agreed with the RPD that the Applicant was credible, CJNG could find him nationwide, and an IFA to Meridian is available, the earlier decision-maker found.

propositions.text: The CJNG's motivation was critical to the RAD's conclusion.
propositions.quote: The motivation of the CJNG was critical to the RAD’s conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The CJNG's motivation was critical to the RAD's conclusion, the earlier decision-maker found.

propositions.text: The RAD unreasonably concluded threats were localized to Veracruz and that risk remained in Yucatan.
propositions.quote: The Applicant now argues that the RAD unreasonably concluded that the threats from the CJNG were localized to Veracruz and that he would remain at risk in Yucatan.

propositions.text: The RAD unreasonably interpreted and applied item 7.7 of the NDP about CJNG operations and scope.
propositions.quote: He submits that the RAD unreasonably interpreted and applied item 7.7 of the National Documentation Package (the “NDP”) which discusses the operations and scope of the CJNG.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the RAD unreasonably localized threats and misapplied NDP item 7.7 on CJNG operations, the Applicant submits.

propositions.text: The RAD unreasonably concluded CJNG's lack of attempts to find him means lack of motivation to locate him.
propositions.quote: The Applicant also submits that the RAD unreasonably concluded that since the CJNG had only left letters at his house and did not try to find him, that it is likely not motivated to locate him.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant submits the RAD unreasonably concluded CJNG's lack of attempts to find him shows lack of motivation, the Applicant argues.

propositions.text: The RAD reasonably applied the IFA legal test and the Applicant failed to show relocating to Meridian was unreasonable.
propositions.quote: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”) contends that the RAD reasonably applied the legal test for an IFA, and that the Applicant failed to show that relocating to Meridien was unreasonable, in his circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent contends the RAD reasonably applied the IFA test and the Applicant failed to show relocating was unreasonable.

propositions.text: Following Vavilov, the RAD decision is reviewable on a reasonableness standard.
propositions.quote: Following the decision of the Supreme Court of Canada in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, [2019] 4 S.C.R. 653, the decision of the RAD is reviewable upon the standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD decision is reviewable on a reasonableness standard following Vavilov.

propositions.text: Reasonableness review asks if the decision shows justification, transparency, intelligibility, and fits factual and legal constraints.
propositions.quote: In considering reasonableness, the Court is to ask if the decision under review “bears the hallmarks of reasonableness – justification, transparency and intelligibility – and whether it is justified in relation to the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on the decision”; see Vavilov, supra, at paragraph 99.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains reasonableness review requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and fitting relevant constraints, citing Vavilov.

propositions.text: The IFA test is two-part: no serious persecution possibility in IFA and it is objectively reasonable to seek safety there before Canada.
propositions.quote: The test for an IFA was addressed by the Federal Court of Appeal in Rasaratnam v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1992] 1 F.C. 706 at 710-711 (F.C.A.). The test is two-part and provides as follows: First, the Board must be satisfied that there is no serious possibility of a claimant being persecuted in the IFA. Second, it must be objectively reasonable to expect a claimant to seek safety in a different part of the country before seeking protection in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Rasaratnam for the two-part IFA test: no serious persecution risk and objective reasonableness to seek safety there first.

propositions.text: The Applicant contests how the RAD treated NDP information on CJNG operations and pursuit of non-compliers.
propositions.quote: The Applicant contests the manner in which the RAD treated the information in the NDP about the manner in which the CJNG operates and how it pursues those who do not comply with its demands.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant contests the RAD's treatment of NDP information on CJNG operations and pursuit of non-compliers, the Applicant argues.

propositions.text: The RAD noted CJNG considers target profile before acting and does not pursue extortion objects.
propositions.quote: The RAD noted that the CJNG takes the profile of a target into account before “acting” and that it does not pursue the objects of its extortion demands.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found CJNG considers target profile before acting and does not pursue extortion objects, the earlier decision-maker found.

propositions.text: Huruglica confirms RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness and can draw its own inferences from evidence.
propositions.quote: According to the decision in Huruglica v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [2014] 4 F.C.R. 811 (F.C.), the RAD is authorized to review decisions of the RPD on a correctness standard. It is authorized to conduct its own assessment of the evidence. In my opinion, this means that it is authorized to draw its own “inferences” from the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Huruglica that RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness and can draw its own inferences from evidence.

propositions.text: The conclusions were open to the RAD, which was entitled to assess documentary and Applicant's evidence.
propositions.quote: The conclusions drawn here were open to the RAD. It was entitled to assess the documentary evidence, as well as the evidence of the Applicant.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD was entitled to assess documentary and Applicant's evidence and draw conclusions.

propositions.text: The Applicant raised speculative arguments and failed to show the RAD's conclusions on the first test part were unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I agree with the submissions of the Respondent that the Applicant raised speculative arguments about the interest of the CJNG in him, and he has not shown that the conclusions of the RAD on the first part of the test were unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the Applicant's arguments are speculative and does not find the RAD's conclusions unreasonable.

propositions.text: The RAD noted CJNG's lack of interest in contacting Applicant's family indicates lack of motivation to pursue him.
propositions.quote: The RAD noted that the lack of interest shown by the CJNG in contacting the Applicant’s family since he left Mexico is another indication of a lack of motivation in pursuing him.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found CJNG's lack of interest in contacting Applicant's family indicates lack of motivation to pursue him, the earlier decision-maker found.

propositions.text: The Applicant did not challenge the RAD’s treatment of the second part of the test
propositions.quote: The Applicant did not challenge the RAD’s treatment of the second part of the test.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant did not challenge the RAD’s treatment of the second part of the test.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review will be dismissed
propositions.quote: the application for judicial review will be dismissed.

propositions.text: There is no question for certification
propositions.quote: There is no question for certification.

propositions.text: The judgment is dated February 20, 2026, by Judge E. Heneghan
propositions.quote: "E. Heneghan" Judge FEDERAL COURT ... DATED: February 20, 2026

propositions.text: The hearing took place in Toronto, Ontario on February 5, 2026
propositions.quote: PLACE OF HEARING: Toronto, Ontario DATE OF HEARING: FEBRUARY 5, 2026

propositions.text: The applicant is Francisco Javier Nieves Velazquez and the respondent is the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration
propositions.quote: STYLE OF CAUSE: FRANCISCO JAVIER NIEVES VELAZQUEZ v. THE MINISTER OF CITIZENSHIP AND IMMIGRATION

propositions.text: The applicant is represented by Terry Guerriero and the respondent by Prathima Prashad
propositions.quote: APPEARANCES: Terry Guerriero For The APPLICANT Prathima Prashad For The Respondent

propositions.text: The applicant's solicitor is Terry Guerriero Barrister & Solicitor; the respondent's solicitor is the Attorney General of Canada, Toronto, Ontario
propositions.quote: SOLICITORS OF RECORD: Terry Guerriero Barrister & Solicitor For The APPLICANT Attorney General of Canada Toronto, Ontario For The Respondent

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the judicial review application, finds no certification question, identifies parties, counsel, hearing date, and judge.
